A key step in this process involves solving an inverse problem to determine the structure's displacement when only the acoustic pressure is known. This problem is classified as ill-posed, meaning that small changes in the data can lead to significantly different outcomes. A heuristic approach is also presented to approximate the solution when the regularized operator is unknown. This method is applied to a physical experiment involving a rectangular panel in an enclosure, demonstrating its effectiveness in reconstructing the panel's deformation when struck by a sound wave. The results show that the reconstructed displacement closely matches the actual deformation, verified through optical measurements.
